input.label: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
input.reasoning_summary:
After investigating potential challenges to the initial verdict, the conclusion remains INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.

H1 (Product cycle attribution): E12 confirms that Greater China growth was "due to higher net sales of iPhone," and E9 discusses general product cycle effects on sales. However, neither passage explicitly attributes the Greater China performance to a NEW product launch or characterizes it as a one-time product cycle effect. The evidence shows iPhone drove the growth but does not specify whether this was from a new model launch versus sustained demand. This does not provide sufficient evidence to contradict the claim.

H2 (Forward-looking sustainability): No evidence was found containing management commentary, guidance, or forward-looking statements characterizing the Greater China performance as sustainable, durable, or representing a recovery. The retrieved passages (E10, E11, E12) provide only factual descriptions of segment definitions and historical performance drivers, without interpretive or forward-looking language about durability.

H3 (Temporary factors): No evidence was found indicating that Greater China growth was driven by channel inventory changes, promotional activities, or other temporary/one-time factors. E13 discusses general product introduction effects on channel inventory but does not specifically link this to Greater China's Q1 2026 performance.

The claim asserts that Greater China results reflect a "durable recovery rather than a one-time product cycle effect." While the evidence confirms strong Greater China performance (38% growth) driven by iPhone, it contains no management discussion characterizing the nature or expected sustainability of this performance. Without explicit filing statements addressing durability versus product cycle effects, the evidence remains insufficient to support or contradict this interpretive claim.
